findings.title: Public measures and the measure of return
findings.claim: In 19:73, rival groups ask which is better by station and gathering; 19:74 adds the furnishings and appearance of earlier generations who were destroyed, and 19:75 ends the apparent extension of the misguided in a weaker force. The focus repeats khayr but places its measure عند ربك and specifies recompense and return. The comparison therefore moves from public standing, company, possessions, and appearance to what returns from action and where its bearer returns, while the preceding verses also show that visible abundance and support do not secure that outcome.
findings.mechanism: The repeated comparative khayr supplies the contact: the earlier question attaches superiority to maqam and nadi, while 19:74 supplies athath and riya and 19:75 names a weak jund. In 19:76, عند ربك relocates the valuation and thawab and marad specify the returned consequence and endpoint. The channel's station and appearance carriers meet these focus terms; the later weak-force cue exposes the limit of display as security.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see both the change in comparison unit and the short pericope movement from public display to its exposed limits and then to lasting deeds, reward, and return.
findings.containment: This does not claim that the rivals' station is lexically a price, that the focus names the same group as 19:75, or that every worldly possession is worthless. The comparison remains an additional pericope reading alongside the primary claim that enduring good deeds are better in reward and return; عند ربك may mark the later plane of valuation without making the earlier boasts a direct quotation of the focus.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel supports the material/status image and the focus surface is fully supplied. The exact HFT metric roles are verified against supplied Arabic anchors but remain attributed because context morphology is not provided.

findings.title: Durability, return, and a provisioned route
findings.claim: The focus measures increase in guidance alongside good deeds that remain, then calls their recompense and return better. The preceding promise held unseen, provision recurring morning and evening, and garden passed as inheritance let the enduring deeds read as an effect carried across absence, repeated time, and succession until it returns as outcome. The supplied journey analogy adds a second contour: guidance is direction, the remaining good is a reserve, and the paired return terms give it an endpoint; 19:62 supplies provision and 19:71 supplies an unavoidable arrival. The travel-reserve picture remains exploratory.
findings.mechanism: The focus's baqiyat carrier meets the promise, recurring provision, and inheritance sequence; thawab and marad meet each other as recompense and return and then contact the pericope's arrival. The h-d-y direction and z-y-d increase supply the route and its growth, while rizq at 19:62 and warid at 19:71 activate the separate travel-provision analogy. These relations make the focus's measures temporally carried and returned rather than immediate possession.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the closing terms gather duration, an outcome sent back, and a final return into one valuation; an exploratory journey image makes the increase and its reserve more concrete.
findings.containment: The journey image is not the lexical translation of يزيد, and the focus does not state that its good deeds are literal supplies. The broader return reading leaves the primary sense of increased guidance and better recompense intact. The promise/provision/inheritance sequence supports durable efficacy but does not prove that each focus act is identical to the promised garden.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel supports the temporal relation and the focus surface is supplied. The more surprising travel-provision contact relies on exact but legacy-unbound HFT roles and is explicitly limited to an analogy.

findings.claim: After the inherited successors in 19:59 squander what they received and follow desire, 19:60 marks out a person who turns back, believes, and does righteous work. The focus's lasting righteous acts can therefore be read as repair that survives a cycle of inherited neglect, not only as a stable class of good deeds.
findings.mechanism: The focus's bāqiyāt and ṣāliḥāt carriers meet the explicit loss and deviation in 19:59 and the exceptive repair in 19:60. The context supplies a break and reversal; the focus adds continuance, so the repaired course can remain after the moment of reversal.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the focus's lasting good deeds as a continuity restored after the pericope has named how continuity can be lost.
findings.containment: This is an attributed contextual reading. The text does not explicitly identify the guided people of 19:76 with the exception in 19:60, and the neighboring verses could contrast outcomes without defining the focus's acts as repair.

epistemic.reason: The Arabic anchors and traced root/word positions are supplied and align with the projected occurrences, but the contextual role assignments and changed reading remain legacy-unbound HFT evidence.

findings.title: Return as differentiated passage
findings.claim: The pericope says all will reach an arrival fixed by decree in 19:71, then 19:72 distinguishes the guarded who are delivered from the wrongdoers left there. The focus's better recompense and return can therefore carry a further reading: a better return names not only an endpoint but the passage and outcome by which one reaches it.
findings.mechanism: The focus's thawab and marad carriers meet the independent arrival, binding decree, rescue, and protection roles traced at 19:71-72. The sequence changes return from a bare destination into an attributed path through an unavoidable encounter whose outcomes separate.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the focus's repeated better measure in light of the immediately preceding account of arrival and differentiated outcome.
findings.containment: This is an attributed contextual reading, not a claim that marad lexically means rescue or that the focus specifies the geography of the passage. A live alternative is that marad names the final destination independently of 19:71-72; the primary return/destination sense remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The context Arabic and HFT word/root coordinates agree with supplied occurrence data. The branch records for the contextual roles are unresolved, so the relation is retained as attributed evidence.

findings.title: Extension and increase as divergent trajectories
findings.claim: The immediately preceding verse lets the person in misguidance be extended until the promised encounter exposes weakness; the focus then says God increases the guidance of those already guided. Together they form an attributed contrast: one course is prolonged until disclosure, while the guided course receives genuine growth and can continue into the focus's better return.
findings.mechanism: The contextual carriers for misguidance, extension, promise, and weakness meet the focus's increase and guidance carriers. This creates two trajectories with different endpoints: 19:75's extension delays exposure, while 19:76's increase develops guidance; the focus's remaining good and return make the positive trajectory durable.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the opening increase of 19:76 as a counter-trajectory to the extension just described, not merely as an isolated statement of more guidance.
findings.containment: The mechanism remains an attributed reading. A live alternative is that madda in 19:75 denotes respite rather than reinforcement or compounding. The focus still says what it says about increased guidance and better recompense; the contrast does not replace either primary statement.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic anchors and traced word/root coordinates are supplied. The feedback structure and the directional inference are attributed HFT interpretations, with the respite alternative retained.

findings.title: A petition beside increased guidance
findings.claim: The focus says that God increases guidance for those already guided. Beside the added petition in 1:6, “Guide us to the straight path,” that increase can be heard as the deepening of what the prayer asks for: direction is requested and then appears at the focus as something that can grow.
findings.mechanism: The focus's guidance words carry the focus return, while the separately added h-d-y imperative at 1:6 supplies the request as an independent trigger. Their contact changes the focus's increase from an isolated benefit into an answer-like progression from asking for direction to receiving more of it.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear requested guidance as continuing and deepening after it is received.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory overlay, not a claim that 1:6 is the historical or direct cause of 19:76, or that the focus describes the same individual supplicants. The native pericope already supplies guidance language; this external ayah adds only the petition-to-increase relation.

epistemic.reason: The external ayah and the focus words are directly supplied with their root occurrences. The petition-to-increase relation is an interpretive recitational inference rather than a packet-stated causal link.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus gives the prayer an answer-like continuation: direction asked for may be received and increased.
branch_activations.boundary: No causal, chronological, or individual identity claim links the two ayat.
